questions.q: Match each scenario to the Act it breaches.
pairs: Someone guesses a colleague's password and reads their email
A company keeps customers' addresses for years after they have left
A pupil uploads a film to a website for anyone to download
questions.feedback: Unauthorised access is the Computer Misuse Act; keeping data too long is the Data Protection Act; sharing somebody else's work is copyright.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.6 Lesson 3 — Law court, station 4: Which Act applies?

questions.q: Which of these are principles of the Data Protection Act 2018? Tick all that apply.
options: Data must be used fairly, lawfully and transparently
Data must be accurate and kept up to date
Data must be kept no longer than necessary
Data must be stored in alphabetical order
Data must be sold only to approved companies
correct: Data must be used fairly, lawfully and transparently
Data must be accurate and kept up to date
Data must be kept no longer than necessary
questions.feedback: The principles are about how data is treated, not about how it is sorted or sold.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.6 Lesson 3 — Law court, station 4: Which Act applies?

questions.q: State what the Computer Misuse Act 1990 makes illegal.

markPoints.concept: gaining access to a computer or data without permission
accept: without permission|unauthorised|unauthorized|not allowed|no right|no permission|without authority|no authority|without consent|not authorised
markPoints.exemplar: Gaining access to a computer or its data without permission.

questions.example: Gaining access to a computer or to data without permission, and doing so in order to commit a further offence or to modify the data.
questions.paraphrase: Getting into a system or its files when you have no authority to do so.
questions.feedback: Access without permission. The Act has three levels, and all of them start there.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.6 Lesson 3 — Law court, station 4: Which Act applies?

questions.q: A student writes a program for coursework and a classmate copies it and submits it as their own. Which Act is most relevant?
questions.feedback: The program is the student's own work, and copying it without permission breaches copyright.
